# specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md

```markdown
> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its
> reconcile step; route each unticked stage per its ROUTING line; never plan
> this document wholesale.

# ces-revisions — roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06 (O1–O6 drawn from specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md Parts A–B, confirmed and ranked by your partner). Background: specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-chatgpt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-claude.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-gemini.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14, managed with uv (.python-version, uv.lock).
Choices made: Bayesian estimation in Python/JAX (NumPyro), per specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md Part C.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release | A | 1 | Release calendar and monthly vintages: a day or two to assemble; public release dates and archived prints. Fit time: measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month revisions comes from late sample reports, and how much from seasonal-factor revision | A | 2 | Needs NSA and SA vintages together; assembly on top of Stage 1's panel unknown until Stage 1 reports; fit time scaled from Stage 1's measured fit |
| O2 | How the size of the two-month revision moves with the first-closing collection rate | A | 3 | Collection-rate series from archived releases: unknown until tried; fit time scaled from Stage 1's measured fit |
| O6 | How revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition | B | 1 | Several days to hand-build from archived releases and technical notes; fit time: measured by Stage 2 |
| O4 | How revision size moves with real BLS appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns | B | 2 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications and appropriations records |
| O5 | How revision size moves with BLS staffing counts | B | 3 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications and federal employment reports |

Tracks: A — collection interval and revision size (research). B — budget, staffing and attrition (research). Track ranking: A, then B.
Split from A because B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built, and B's answer does not change Track A's model; A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision size
      Objective: Show, on real CES vintages, how the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release.
      Outcomes: O1
      Track: A
      Consumes: nothing (the package is a scaffold)
      Produces: the monthly CES vintage panel (first, second and third prints, benchmarks) and the release calendar with collection days, readable by later stages; specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: The findings file reports the estimated relation between collection days and one-month revision size, with its uncertainty, on the real monthly vintages; it records the measured cost of the real run: assembly time, data volume and model-fit wall time.
      Leaves out: validation suite: suggested, see the approval question; provenance manifest: suggested, see the approval question
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Sample size, attrition and revision size
      Objective: Show, on real CES vintages, how revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition.
      Outcomes: O6
      Track: B
      Consumes: the monthly CES vintage panel from Stage 1
      Produces: the CES sample size and attrition series, readable by later stages; specs/ces-revisions-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: The findings file reports the estimated relation between sample size and attrition and revision size, with its uncertainty, on the real monthly vintages; it records the measured cost of the real run: hand-build time for the series and model-fit wall time.
      Leaves out: validation suite: suggested, see the approval question; provenance manifest: suggested, see the approval question
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Ranked list — Track A

1. O3 — NSA and SA vintages together; assembly unknown until Stage 1 reports; fit time scaled from Stage 1
2. O2 — collection-rate series from archived releases, unknown until tried; fit time scaled from Stage 1

## Ranked list — Track B

1. O4 — several days to hand-build from budget justifications and appropriations records
2. O5 — several days to hand-build from budget justifications and federal employment reports

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every committed stage is ticked and each Ranked list is empty (promoted, or parked when its track stops), re-run the gap rubric over the Outcomes list (O1–O6, plus any approved outcomes), with evidence per verdict: implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, and specs/deferred_items.md entries. Unmet outcomes exit as a new stage or a conscious deferral with a written why.
```

Approve this partition (Stage 1, Track A core on O1; then Stage 2, Track B core on O6, which reads Stage 1's vintage panel), and two qualities I suggest for both tracks' Ranked lists: a **validation suite**, because the brief's Part C requires LOO/PSIS against a constant-variance baseline and pseudo-real-time checks (outcome: "each finding checked against a constant-variance baseline and in pseudo-real time"), and a **provenance manifest**, because the vintages and hand-built covariates must trace to their source releases and budget pages (outcome: "every input series traceable to its source document"). If you approve either, where does it rank in each track?
